builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
summary: It replaces keyword-matching tool-use benchmarks with verbatim-reproduction checks, a first-token prior probe, and embedding-drift checks. The diagnostic ladder costs minutes of CPU time; the optional repair is about 2,202 SFT steps and roughly 3.3 GPU-hours, feasible on one 24 GB GPU. After adoption, models can still over-trigger on negative prompts, suppression benefits remain seed-sensitive, and passing format diagnostics does not prove end-task correctness.
rationale: It is immediately usable on constrained infrastructure and prevents false production claims about tool use before expensive integration or evaluation decisions are made.
technique: Strict cheap diagnostics for tool-use claims

claims.statement: It replaces keyword-matching tool-use benchmarks with verbatim-reproduction checks, a first-token prior probe, and embedding-drift checks. The diagnostic ladder costs minutes of CPU time; the optional repair is about 2,202 SFT steps and roughly 3.3 GPU-hours, feasible on one 24 GB GPU. After adoption, models can still over-trigger on negative prompts, suppression benefits remain seed-sensitive, and passing format diagnostics does not prove end-task correctness.
Targeted repair raises valid tool-call emission from 0.100 to 0.959 on corpus rows and unseen-prompt pass rate from 0.428 to 0.536 versus the stronger baseline (p=0.004).
